verdict.rationale: Letta's own SDK lets a developer seed an agent's memory with arbitrary entries, each stored as a Markdown file in the memory repository, and /init builds memory by inspecting a repository. So non-transcript content can enter memory through documented paths. No dedicated pipeline for ingesting documents, JSON, or business data is documented. Missing for 10: a documented ingestion API or loader for documents, files and JSON/structured business data; format handling and chunking details; independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can ingest documents, JSON, and business data into memory — not just chat transcripts

citations.quote: Pass memory for full control over the agent’s starting memory. Each entry becomes a Markdown file in the agent’s memory repository
Run `/init` to bootstrap or refresh memory for the current project. The agent inspects the repository
Shared memory gives multiple agents access to the same files and working context.
Letta's memory management is primarily text/files based so very transparent and controllable.
